decisions.decision: How should source documents enter the workflow?
decisions.context: Millions of documents arrive daily, but the brief does not require predictions at request time. The ingestion path must handle volume while feeding repeatable classification runs.

alternatives.label: ETL-based feature ingestion
pros: High volume: batch extraction and transformation
cons: Freshness: waits for the next load

decisions.rationale: Daily volume favors batch loading, consistent with the scalable data processing described in “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture.” This gives up immediate ingestion freshness, which the brief does not require.
consequences: Size batch windows to seasonal peaks.

decisions.context: The classifier must process millions of documents, and several teams consume its results. The brief sets no per-document response-time target.

alternatives.label: Scheduled batch prediction deployment
pros: High volume: scores large sets in scheduled runs
Multiple consumers: writes results to shared storage
cons: Freshness: results wait for a run

decisions.rationale: High daily volume decides the choice: scheduled scoring can write results for multiple teams to consume, as described in “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “System Architectures for Personalization and Recommendation.” This gives up immediate results; the brief provides no latency requirement to justify online serving.
consequences: Teams consume persisted results after each run.
Batch failures can delay results for every consumer.

decisions.decision: How should runtime capacity respond to seasonal demand?
decisions.context: Document volume varies strongly over the year, so fixed capacity risks either peak-time bottlenecks or idle resources outside peaks.

alternatives.label: Elastic resource scaling
pros: Seasonal capacity: compute follows workload demand
High volume: expands for large jobs
cons: Cost: peak capacity may be expensive

alternatives.label: Scale-to-zero serving
cons: Seasonal capacity: startup can delay work

decisions.rationale: Seasonal capacity swings decide the choice: elastic scaling fits variable workloads, as described in “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture.” It may cost more during peaks than scaling to zero, but keeps capacity available when document volume rises.
consequences: Set scaling limits for peak periods.
Monitor queue depth and job completion time.
Provisioning changes can lag sudden demand spikes.

decisions.decision: How should production quality and drift be monitored?
decisions.context: Operators need visibility when classification quality drifts. The brief does not state how quickly labels or quality measurements become available.

alternatives.label: Input and feature-drift monitoring
pros: Drift visibility: detects changes in inputs and distributions
cons: Classification quality: drift does not prove accuracy loss

alternatives.label: Real-time prediction-quality monitoring
pros: Classification quality: measures model behavior when labels are available
cons: Drift visibility: quality signal may arrive late

alternatives.label: Passive production operation
cons: Drift visibility: operators may miss degradation

decisions.rationale: Drift visibility decides the choice: input monitoring gives operators a signal about changing document data, as described in “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning.” It cannot establish that accuracy has fallen, so prediction quality should also be measured when labels become available.
consequences: Track input distributions and schema changes.
Retain predictions and eventual labels for quality checks.
Define which drift signals require investigation.

decisions.decision: How should ML workflow stages be coordinated?
decisions.context: At this volume, repeated classification runs need dependable preparation, scoring, and evaluation stages. Teams also need a consistent workflow to operate and evolve the system.

alternatives.label: Orchestrated ML pipeline
cons: Cost: requires pipeline setup and maintenance

alternatives.label: Manual script-driven workflow
cons: High volume: manual transitions limit repeatability

decisions.rationale: Repeatable operation decides the choice: an orchestrated pipeline connects recurring stages, as described in “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning.” This costs more to establish than manual scripts, but supports frequent, consistent runs.
consequences: Failures require retry and alert policies.
The ingestion mechanism must be decided first.

decisions.decision: How should teams access classification results?
decisions.context: Several teams consume the classifications, so the system needs a shared integration boundary. Since the selected prediction mode is batch, an API can expose persisted results without requiring online scoring.

alternatives.label: REST prediction microservice
pros: Integration: separates callers from model implementation
cons: High volume: request traffic can burden serving

decisions.rationale: Multiple consumers decide the choice: a REST interface offers a shared application boundary, as described in “How to power up your product by machine learning with python microservice” and “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline.” The service exposes completed batch results; it does not require synchronous scoring for every document.
consequences: Publish a stable result schema and access contract.
Control access for each consuming team.
Persist batch outputs behind the service.

Retry, deduplication, ordering, and failure recovery for document ingestion.
Result retention, access controls, and audit requirements for insurer data.
